source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Iron deficiency, which characteristically produces macrocytosis as iron stores fall.","B":"Thalassemia trait, which characteristically produces a high MCV from enlarged red cells.","C":"Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, which can produce megaloblastic macrocytic anemia.","D":"Anemia of chronic disease, which is defined by marked macrocytosis from folate trapping."}}
source_row.rationale: An MCV above the reference range indicates macrocytosis. Low vitamin B12 or folate can cause macrocytic or megaloblastic anemia, whereas iron deficiency more commonly produces microcytosis.
source_row.source_detail: Macrocytic/megaloblastic anemia evaluation: increased MCV and vitamin B12 or folate deficiency. Live ARUP Consult topic currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential: diagnostic/laboratory interpretation, transfusion risk, postprocedure monitoring, device management and potential complications. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client has anemia with an elevated mean corpuscular volume (MCV). Which deficiency pattern should be considered?
